metadata.title: The Effects of Artificial Intelligence on the Future of Employment

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper does not conduct an original ILSA micro-data analysis; it is a narrative literature review about AI and employment. Because no student-level assessment dataset (e.g., PIAAC) is analyzed with sampling-based estimation, there is no application of ILSA complex survey weights (e.g., student weights or replicate weights) and no need to specify weight variables. Consequently, plausible values and missing-data handling for achievement scales are not part of the study’s methodology. For future empirical work using PIAAC, analysts should apply the official student weights and replicate weights provided by the data producer when estimating population-representative statistics, and they should follow the assessment’s documented plausible-values procedure for cognitive domains.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the article does not analyze student-level cognitive achievement outcomes from an ILSA assessment (e.g., PIAAC) using PV-based scoring. Instead, it synthesizes prior research and reports high-level employment-related estimates from external sources (e.g., ILO and other studies) without fitting PV-based models. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no original dataset construction or statistical estimation pipeline in the paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA micro-data sample is constructed or filtered. The paper synthesizes findings from prior studies and external reports; therefore, there is no analytic subsample definition (e.g., grade/domain filters, task completion criteria, or missingness exclusions) for student-level assessment data.

data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the manuscript is not an empirical ILSA-based ML study: it contains no student-level dataset, no model training, and no reported sampling/weighting or PV/missing-data procedures. As a result, fields such as total sample size, country-level Ns, ML algorithms, and performance metrics cannot be populated without inventing details not present in the provided text.
